text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A27, A36, A37 and A42 each ran in every one of the 200 cases (participation 100%, about one occurrence per case). In the later window, each runs in only about half of the cases — A27 in about 54 in 100, A36 in about 47, A37 and A42 in about 48 — with mean occurrences per case falling to roughly 0.5. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- A27 and the three activities A36, A37 and A42, which always appeared together before (co-occurrence in 200 of 200 cases, with the trio running before A27 in about 99 in 100), now almost never share a case: co-occurrence in about 1 in 100 cases or fewer, with A27 alone in about 52–53 in 100 cases and a trio activity alone in about 47. [REL011, REL012, REL013]
- The trio still moves as one unit: in the later window, any two of A36, A37 and A42 co-occur in about 47 in 100 cases and neither appears in about 52, with virtually no single-only cases; their mutual order stays mixed (about 21 versus 25 in 100 of all cases, like the roughly even split before). [REL020, REL021, REL022]
- A25 previously spread its outgoing transitions almost evenly over A42 (about 35 in 100), A36 (about 33) and A37 (about 31); in the later window, about 99 in 100 go to A28, and the A25-to-A28 distance shrank from four to five event positions (about 94 in 100 at four) to one position (about 98 in 100). [DIR001, LAG001]
- The trio changed sides relative to A28 and A26: before, each trio activity preceded A28 in about 99 in 100 shared cases and preceded A26 in about 98–99 in 100; in the later window, A28 precedes the trio and A26 precedes the trio in about 46–47 in 100 cases each. A26's own transitions, previously almost only to A27 (about 97–98 in 100), now split between A27 (about 52 in 100) and the trio (about 14–17 in 100 each). [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016, DIR002]
- The trio now feeds A31 directly: before, A36, A37 and A42 led to one another and to A28 (roughly 26–38 in 100 each) and reached A31 only indirectly; in the later window, each sends about 28–36 in 100 of its transitions straight to A31. Accordingly, the A26-to-A31 distance, previously two positions in about 96–97 in 100 cases, is now two positions in about 51 in 100 (via A27) and four positions in about 46 in 100 (via the three trio activities). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL017, REL018, REL019, LAG005]
- The frame around the branches is unchanged in participation: A25, A26, A28 and A31 still run in every later case — for example, A31 co-occurs with A27 in about 54 in 100 later cases and is the only one of that pair in about 47, and A28 runs without the trio in about 52–53 in 100. [REL001, REL005, REL009, REL010, REL014]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural re-routing of the segment A36–A37–A42. In the earlier window, every case ran A25, then the trio A36–A37–A42 in mixed order, then A28, with A26 followed by A27 and A31 later in the case; the trio always preceded A27. In the later window, A25 leads almost exclusively to A28 (about 99 in 100 of its transitions, one position away), and A26 routes each case into exactly one of two mutually exclusive branches: A27 alone (about 53 in 100 cases) or the trio (about 47 in 100 cases), which now sits between A26 and A31 and leads directly to A31. Read as a possibility supported by the evidence, the trio became optional, moved from before A28 to between A26 and A31, and changed from a mandatory predecessor of A27 into its alternative. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, LAG001, LAG005]

The hypothesis is shown directly rather than inferred from frequencies alone: relational items capture the collapse of A27–trio co-occurrence from all cases to about 1 in 100, directional items capture the rewired successors (A25 to A28, A26 to the trio, the trio to A31), and distance items capture A25–A28 tightening from four positions to one while A26–A31 splits into two and four positions, matching the two branches. Chance is an unlikely explanation for the pattern as a whole: 42 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.68 expected if nothing had changed — many times that expectation — and every item's difference was larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the pooled data. [REL011, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, LAG001, LAG005, OCC001]

Limitations: all indicators use event positions rather than elapsed time, so the change is established in sequence structure only. The evidence cannot show what decides which branch a case takes, and it cannot fully exclude that the optional branch existed before the change point at a rate too low for the 200 earlier cases to sample — although a pre-existing split near fifty-fifty is incompatible with all 200 earlier cases showing the mandatory trio. [REL002, REL011, OCC002]

Other differences: only trace-level residuals — isolated outgoing edges at about 0.5 in 100 transitions that appear in one window each (for example A25 to A12 or A24 in the later window, A25 to A09 or A10 in the earlier one), and A27 occurring twice within a case in about 1 in 100 later cases. [DIR001, DIR002, OCC001]
